content: I am interested in working on some formalization projects in algebraic geometry to get an idea of where mathlib has reached these days and what can be done easily with AI tools. Does anyone have any advice on how I would get started for instance in proving that an injective module M over a Noetherian ring A gives rise to a flasque sheaf of O_X-modules on X = Spec A. This is Hartshorne chapter 3, prop 3.4. The proof involves for example Noetherian induction and the support of a module and the support of a section. Is this result already in mathlib? If not are the necessary preliminaries in mathlib?
There are human contibutors to mathlib that are working towards proving results about the cohomology of quasi-coherent sheaves. My advice is "Do not use AI to formalise this".

Thank you for your comment. I have made a PR #42113, where I prove one small commutative algebra lemma ( Lemma III.3.3 of Hartshorne). I used Claude to explain things to me and to help me find names of lemmas and deifnitions in mathlib. So I am trying to use AI to help me understand lean code and not just generate everything. I would be very grateful to anyone who has a look at what I wrote and shares any feedback with me.
